## Workload
- Single visible template q01 = TPC-H Q1 shape: scan lineitem with one range filter on a date (selects ~98%),
  4 groups (2 string keys -> compressed to utinyint), 4 sum_no_overflow + 3 avg + count_star on DECIMAL(int64).
- Baseline 363ms wall. Operator CPU (profile, summed over threads): TABLE_SCAN 2.44s, PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY 1.72s,
  projections 0.23 + 0.05 + 0.21s.
- Types: l_* decimals DECIMAL(15,2) int64; products DECIMAL(18,4)/(18,6) still int64; sum results DECIMAL(38,x)
  but executed as sum_no_overflow (int64 state, chosen from stats). avg on decimal int64 uses AvgState<hugeint_t>
  with AddToHugeint (branchless, cheap) - not the bottleneck by itself.

## Codebase facts
- Perfect hash agg: src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp AddChunk: per-row address, then
  RowOperations::UpdateStates (scatter) per aggregate + AddInPlace on addresses after each aggregate.
- Scatter/simple update loops: src/include/duckdb/common/vector_operations/aggregate_executor.hpp
  (UnaryScatterLoop, UnaryFlatUpdateLoop with __restrict state).
- simple_update callback: AggregateFunction::GetStateSimpleUpdateCallback(); signature
  (Vector inputs[], AggregateInputData&, idx_t input_count, data_ptr_t state, idx_t count).
- RowOperations::UpdateStates in src/common/row_operations/row_aggregate.cpp builds
  AggregateInputData(aggr.GetFunctionData(), allocator).
- avg / sum impls in extension/core_functions/aggregate/{algebraic/avg.cpp,distributive/sum.cpp},
  helpers in extension/core_functions/include/core_functions/aggregate/sum_helpers.hpp.
- dbe-tool sql: selecting typeof(col) w/o aggregate errors; wrap in any_value().

## Round log
- G1R1: dispatched "Perfect-hash aggregate: per-group simple_update for few distinct groups per chunk"
  (hypothesis: serial memory RMW chain in scatter for few groups). Backlog: fuse stacked projections (needs investigation).

## Ideas not yet explored
- Scan (2.44s CPU, biggest): filter pushdown on date with ~98% selectivity -> other columns fetched via
  selection; check if a near-full selection could scan flat and skip sel (look at column_segment / scan filter code).
- Decimal multiply in projections: check overflow-check cost in decimal multiply (could use stats to skip checks).

issues.title: Perfect-hash aggregate: per-group simple_update for few distinct groups per chunk
issues.hypothesis: In q01 PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY costs 1.72s CPU over 58.8M rows (~29ns/row for 8 aggregates), second only to the scan. PerfectAggregateHashTable::AddChunk (src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp:117) computes a per-row state address and calls the scatter update (AggregateExecutor::UnaryScatterLoop) once per aggregate, then VectorOperations::AddInPlace on the address vector after each aggregate. With only a handful of groups, consecutive rows hit the same state address, so every aggregate's loop is a serial read-modify-write chain through memory (store-to-load forwarding latency, no register accumulation, no vectorisation), plus 8 extra passes over the address vector. The simple_update path (UnaryFlatUpdateLoop/UnaryUpdateLoop in src/include/duckdb/common/vector_operations/aggregate_executor.hpp) takes a single __restrict state pointer, letting the compiler keep the accumulator in registers.
issues.plan: In PerfectAggregateHashTable::AddChunk, after computing group indices (before converting to addresses), count rows per group index for this chunk. If the number of distinct groups present in the chunk is small (e.g. <= 8, and every aggregate has no filter and a non-null simple_update callback via aggregate.function.GetStateSimpleUpdateCallback()), do a stable counting-sort of row indices into one SelectionVector per present group (single pass, preserves input order within a group so order-sensitive aggregates such as first/list/string_agg and float sums give identical results). Set group_is_set for those groups. Then for each present group g and each aggregate: slice the aggregate's payload input vectors with the group's selection (Vector::Slice(vec, sel, cnt) into a temp vector, or DataChunk::Slice on a reference copy), and call simple_update(inputs, AggregateInputData(aggregate.GetFunctionData(), *aggregate_allocator), child_count, data + g*tuple_size + aggregate_offset, cnt). Count_star (child_count 0) passes nullptr inputs as UpdateStates does. Keep the bounds check / InvalidInputException for group >= total_groups. If the distinct count exceeds the threshold or any aggregate is filtered / lacks simple_update, fall back to the existing scatter path unchanged. Optionally special-case: if all rows of the chunk belong to one group, skip slicing entirely and call simple_update on the payload directly.
issues.expected_gain: q01: aggregation CPU 1.72s -> maybe 0.8-1.0s, i.e. ~15-20% of total query CPU (~300ms -> ~250-300ms wall).
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY on low-cardinality integer/small-domain keys that the optimizer routes to the perfect hash aggregate (flags, status codes, booleans, small enums, years) with many sum/avg/count/min/max aggregates. Queries with many distinct groups per chunk see only the cost of a per-chunk distinct count (cheap) and take the old path.
issues.risk: Medium-low. Correctness risks: preserving order within groups (stable sort required), NULL handling (simple_update handles validity through the sliced vector's unified format), aggregates whose simple_update differs semantically from update (should not exist). Performance risk: dictionary slicing overhead per group per aggregate for chunks with ~8 groups; threshold limits it.

issues.title: Fuse stacked projections between scan and aggregate
issues.hypothesis: q01 has three PROJECTION operators over 58.8M rows between TABLE_SCAN and the aggregate (0.23s + 0.05s compress_string + 0.21s = ~0.5s CPU). The first computes l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount), the third recomputes #4*(1+l_tax) and re-references columns; each projection materialises vectors. Merging adjacent projections (or avoiding the compress-string projection being inserted between them) would save per-chunk overhead and copies.
issues.plan: Investigate where the compressed-materialization optimizer (src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*) inserts the __internal_compress_string projection under an aggregate whose groups are already small, and whether a projection-merge step exists (RemoveUnusedColumns / common subexpression). Needs investigation before implementation.
issues.generality: Any aggregate over computed expressions with string group keys.
issues.risk: Medium; optimizer change, needs more investigation.
